cards.text: This psalm comes from the sons of Korah, written for the choirmaster. And friend, it does NOT ease you in. No warm-up, no soft intro, just a call to clap your hands and shout to God.

cards.question: The psalm opens with a call to clap and shout to God. Who does it call on to do it?

cards.text: And this is not polite little golf clapping. This is shouting to God with a voice of triumph, because how awesome is the LORD Most High!

cards.question: The psalm calls the LORD Most High a great King. How far does His rule reach?

answers.text: Only over the land of Israel
Only over the city of Zion

cards.text: Then the psalm gets into what this great King does for His people. Me? I needed help just getting out of a junk drawer.

cards.question: True or false: the psalm says God subdues nations beneath His people.

cards.text: Next comes an inheritance, and an old name: Jacob, the father of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 49:28).

cards.question: True or false: the psalm says God's people pick out their own inheritance.
God chooses the inheritance, the pride of Jacob, whom He ___.

cards.text: Then comes a Selah. After it, God has ascended, and the whole crowd is shouting for joy.

cards.question: God goes up amid shouts of joy. What sound goes up with Him?

cards.text: Sing praises to God. Sing praises. Sing praises to our King. Sing praises! Four times, friend, like my oven timer when I pretend I didn't hear it the first three.

cards.question: After all those calls to sing praises, the psalm gives the reason. What is it?

answers.text: God is King of all the earth
God has sent rain on the land
God has ended the long famine

cards.text: Then the psalm says it plain: God reigns over the nations. This King does not clock out at five.

cards.question: True or false: the psalm pictures God seated on His holy throne.

cards.text: The last verse opens on a gathering: the nobles of the nations have assembled. That's a guest list where EVERY name comes with a title.

cards.question: The nobles of the nations assemble as the people of which God?

cards.text: That's Abraham, the man God told that all the families of the earth would be blessed through him (Genesis 12:3).

cards.question: The psalm says the shields of the earth belong to ___.

cards.text: And the psalm lands right here: He is highly exalted. I went from a 25 cent bin to my own bakery, so I know a little about getting lifted up, but friend, NOBODY gets lifted higher than Him.

findings.problem: The card says the shouting happens "because how awesome is the LORD Most High!" The BSB text of 47:1-2 has no "because" or "for" linking the call to shout with the line about how awesome the LORD is. The card adds a reason the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with "Only over..." and the right answer doesn't. The pattern makes the right answer stand out as the odd one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card tells no part of the passage. It is a transition line plus a joke, and it cites Psalm 47:2 without telling anything from that verse beyond repeating "great King."

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke compares God subduing nations beneath His people to Papa Dorin needing help getting out of a junk drawer. The core actions don't match, so a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "The whole crowd is shouting for joy" stretches the text. Psalm 47:5 says only that God has ascended "amid shouts of joy." No crowd is mentioned, and "whole" is not in the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has five sentences: four short "Sing praises" sentences plus the timer joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
